newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange ended weaker in brisk trading on Wednesday, pulled down by investor profit-taking in every sector except for surging golds.
The TSE's key 300 Composite Index dropped 30.08 points to 5910.65, losing ground for the third day in a row.
Since Monday the 300 index has fallen 106 points or more than 1.7 percent.

"The market is a little shaky right now, and I imagine there's some people taking profits," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie. Market players sold stocks to reap profits after big gains earlier this year.
Trading was brisk with 111 million shares changing hands worth more than C$1.7 billion.
Declining issues beat out advancing ones 581 to 428 while 272 traded unchanged.
"Another one of those middle-cycle corrections," said ScotiaMcLeod senior vice-president Fred Ketchen. "I expect this to be short-lived."
Ketchen said he expected Toronto to continue to rise since investors have nowhere to turn. Fixed income markets generally provide slower returns than equities.
* Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd jumped 1.30 to 20.20 on more than five million shares.

Bre-X said today that it and Barrick Gold Corp have made some progress on an ownership deal over Bre-X's huge Busang gold discovery in Indonesia. The Indonesian government, which advised a joint venture between the two, has not yet extended today's deadline.
* Northern Telecom Ltd fell 2.50 to 84.30 in brisk dealings.
